title: Autodiag Sculptor: generate condensed runbooks and targeted probe packs for on-call
author: Marina Lopez
description:
Motivation: first-response time is dominated by context gathering and noisy playbooks. This PR introduces the 'Autodiag Sculptor' feature in incident-bot which synthesizes a compact runbook, selects a minimal set of telemetry probes, and packages them into a zip that on-call can run or hand off. The goal is to reduce mean time to diagnosis for common infrastructure classes (serving runtime slowdowns, KV-cache misses, model fallback churn).

What this PR does (high-level): - Adds a probe-selection engine that ranks candidate telemetry queries by information gain and cost. - Adds a runbook templating step that produces a 1-page actionable runbook (symptom, quick checks, one-line commands, safe mitigations). - Implements a probe-pack exporter (JSON + shell snippets + sanitized query handles) that incident-bot can attach to Slack/PagerDuty handoff cards. - Adds a small policy store to prefer non-disruptive checks first (read-only metrics/traces before restarts). - Exposes a /api/v1/incident/:id/autodiag endpoint for programmatic request and a CLI helper incident-bot probe pack fetch <incident-id>.

Implementation notes: the probe selector is a lightweight ruleset followed by information-gain scoring using historical incident traces (local LRU cache of signals). We intentionally keep the first rollout heuristic-driven (no ML model) to allow deterministic audits. The templating engine uses Mustache templates and a small domain-specific macro for one-line commands. Probe artifacts are sanitized with a redaction pipeline to strip secrets and internal urls.

Backward compatibility and security: existing incident cards remain unchanged by default; the autodiag endpoint is opt-in per escalation policy. Probe export artifacts are stored in the incident-bot attachment bucket and signed with a short-lived URL. KMS-encrypted audit logs are emitted for each probe-pack generation.

Testing and rollout: unit tests for selector heuristics, integration tests that simulate SOA latency incidents, and an end-to-end smoke test that posts a probe-pack to the #oncall-test Slack channel. Rollout plan: staged opt-in for % of teams, feature-flagged behind ff.autodiag_sculptor.

Checklist: - [x] Add probe selector and scoring logic - [x] Add runbook templates and macros - [x] Add API endpoint and CLI helper - [x] Add attachment upload and signed-url flow - [x] Add audit logging and redaction pipeline - [x] Add unit/integration tests - [x] Update docs (short runbook in ops docs)

Related: references ENG-1482 for oncall time-to-diagnosis analysis and ENG-2029 for sanitized telemetry bundles. Links: internal runbook draft: https://linear.redwood.example/ENG-1482, telemetry schema: docs/telemetry/schema.md

review_thread:
Samir: Nice feature — can you justify why we don't rely on existing evaluation infra to compute information gain?
Marina: We considered the eval infra but it is offline and high-latency; the selector needs to be sub-100ms during generation and the rules+histogram approach gives a deterministic baseline. We plan to add a lightweight async scorer using precomputed artifacts in a follow-up (ENG-2157).
Ava: Security question: what guarantees that queries in probe-packs won't accidentally reference internal-only endpoints?
Marina: All query templates go through redaction and an allowlist; the exporter will reject any probe that contains hostnames outside accepted domains. We've added unit tests for host allowlist and an audit event.
Diego: Tests look good, but add a KPI to measure probe-pack helpfulness (did it reduce TTD) as an event so we can iterate.
Marina: Added an analytics event emission (incident.autodiag.invoked + probe_pack.result_label) in the uploader; tracking ticket ENG-2241 for dashboard.
Samir: CI flakes on Linux build fixed by pinning a dev dependency — approved.
Ava: Approved after small nits fixed.
Mergebot: merged via squash
release_notes: Adds an opt-in 'Autodiag Sculptor' that generates condensed runbooks and minimal probe-packs to accelerate on-call diagnosis. Feature behind ff.autodiag_sculptor; audit-logged and redacted exports.
